- You can now select and copy text while looking at an older version in version history, tables included. Table cells copy as tab-separated text, so they paste into a spreadsheet. The old version still can't be edited.

- You can now drag the Co-writer panel as wide as you like. It used to stop at 560px; now it only stops where the editor would get too narrow to use.

- A new note's name is now its heading. Name it in ⌘N, or rename a new note in the sidebar, and it opens with that title and the caret on the line below, ready to write.

- The editor now checks your spelling. Misspelled words get the standard macOS red underline. Edit › Spelling and Grammar lets you turn it off, check grammar too, or open the spelling panel (⌘:). Automatic spelling correction starts off so macOS doesn't rewrite your markdown, but you can turn it on from the same menu.

- The word count at the bottom of the note hides while version history is open, so it no longer covers the timeline.

- When a long conversation gets too big, Co-writer now tells you it's "Compacting conversation…" instead of looking stuck on "Thinking…". Afterwards, a "Conversation compacted" line marks where it happened: Co-writer only remembers a summary of the messages above it. This works with both Claude and Codex.

- With Claude, type `/compact` in Co-writer to compact the conversation yourself. It now appears in the slash menu, and you can add instructions for what the summary should keep.

- In version history, added words are highlighted in green and removed words are struck through in red. A line that still shows the old wording is not also marked as a new paragraph.
